newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after PPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after PPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening higher on Friday after a weaker-than-forecast report on May producer prices, analysts said. The following are their comments:
PHILIP ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER OF VALUE LINE'S ASSET MANAGEMENT DIVISION:
"These numbers were materially weaker than was expected."

Orlando added: "The momentum players will seize this weaker-than-expected PPI number and, in my opinion, continue to drive equity prices higher. I don't believe that equity prices are justified where they are currently but this market is working on momentum right now and this indicator is exactly what the momentum guys were hoping for."
The Labor Department reported the Producer Price Index dropped 0.3 percent in May after a 0.6 percent drop in April. Economists in a Reuters poll had expected the PPI to rise 0.1 percent in May.
The core PPI, without the volatile food and energy components, fell 0.3 percent in May, after a 0.1 percent decline in April. Economists had expected the core rate to rise 0.1 percent in May.
ALAN ACKERMAN, MARKET STRATEGIST AT FAHNESTOCK & CO:
"Treasuries are up on a May PPI drop...signs of a slowing economy are really raising hopes that the Fed won't raise rates in July."
MICHAEL METZ, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST AT OPPENHEIMER & CO:
"In many respects it is better than expected but in one way it is more disturbing...I think the rise in the crude level is really an ominous sign."
The crude goods component in the PPI rose 1.3 percent in May after an 0.9 percent drop in April.
Metz added: "But (the total PPI report) is more disinflationary than expected" and should push the stock market higher.
The 30-year Treasury bond was up 14/32, its yield dropping to 6.74 percent from Thursday's close at 6.78 percent.
